dispositions.method: The automatic families first printed in 1796 that reach 3 or more papers, long-running ones included, were split into single printed items (story_items.py --long-running, items.json), and the families of 1795 were split again over the 1796 pages (items_from_1795.json). Every item in 3 or more papers was counted by its own opening over all 1,552 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units (46 of 160 met the bar); every page was swept for seven-word sequences shared by 4 or more papers (sweep_new and sweep_recheck: the passages no item covers); every unit and passage that meets the bar was read, with each eligible item's opening checked on every page it counts, and the chosen items' openings were searched over all pages (phrase_hits.json).
dispositions.selection_rule: The thin-year rule (register Y-THIN) as amended by the owner's choice B1 on 23 November 2026: an item, counted by its own words, is eligible when it was printed by more than half of the newspapers that survive for its weeks, and by at least 4; digests are not. As in R-01, items printed by every newspaper that survives for their weeks are admitted, and the other eligible items are chosen to cover the months and the kinds of news, about as many stories as a standard year (about 20 to 35, a target, not a quota); one affair's items as in X-1800-01. The eligible items not chosen are listed with their counts and are not checked against the scans. Sub-stories (C-01), private persons (R-04) and the list of items read and not admitted (R-03) apply as in every year.
dispositions.paper_counting: 1796 has 7 catalogue series, which are 6 papers (C-04): the Gazette of the United States (Philadelphia, under two numbers, the second from 1 July), the New Hampshire Gazette (Portsmouth), the Kentucky Gazette (Lexington), the Federal Mirror (Concord, to November), the Patowmac Guardian (29 issues) and the Eagle, or, Dartmouth Centinel (Hanover, six issues). The release's map lists five misfiled RevX pages for 1796 (the Gazette of the United States of 7 and 31 May, 18 August and 25 November); no chosen printing is on them.

counted_item_by_item.Paper counts: Every finder item of 1796 in 3 or more papers (and of 1795 over the 1796 pages) was counted by its own opening over all 1,552 pages in both transcriptions and merged into text units: 46 of 160 units met the bar. Reading them, with the sweep's passages, gave 162 items: 47 eligible and 115 below the bar. One is printed by every paper that survives for its weeks and is admitted; 27 are chosen (28 stories, 28 groups, 115 printings); 18 eligible items are listed as not chosen and 1 for the owner.
counted_item_by_item.The bar: Y-THIN: more than half of the papers that survive for the item's weeks (a surviving issue between its first and last printing, and at least in the three weeks from its first printing), and at least 4. 1796 has 6 papers: the Gazette of the United States (Philadelphia, daily, under two catalogue numbers), the New Hampshire Gazette and the Kentucky Gazette survive all year, the Federal Mirror to November, the Patowmac Guardian in 29 issues, and the Eagle, or, Dartmouth Centinel in six; 4 or 5 papers are in print in most weeks, 6 when an issue of the Eagle falls in them. The bar is 4.
counted_item_by_item.Counted by their openings: The reading checked every eligible item's opening on each page it counts; this review read every printing of the chosen items again before cutting their excerpts, and their counts stand.
counted_item_by_item.Printed forms together: C-02: the Patowmac Guardian prints the elephant, Captain Atkinson's news and Captain Seward's in its own words; the Kentucky Gazette prints the Baron de Carondelet in its own words and the ratifications of the British treaty without the Charleston paper's words; the Federal Mirror prints the papers on a general peace under its own heading ('Prospect of Peace terminated. London, April 14. The following very IMPORTANT PAPERS, were yesterday communicated') and General Moreau's report as a letter dated 'AMIENS, Aug. 15.'
counted_item_by_item.Printed in parts: The Kentucky Gazette prints the ratifications of the British treaty in two issues (19 and 26 March); the treaty with Spain runs over pages 1 and 2 in three papers. Each printing counts once, by its opening.
counted_item_by_item.One paper under two catalogue numbers: C-04: the Gazette of the United States is sn84026273 to 30 June and sn83025881 from 1 July ('Gazette of the United States, & Philadelphia Daily Advertiser'); it is counted as one paper.

for_user_decision.The papers in print, the bar and the cho: As built: Y-THIN as amended (B1) with 6 papers (7 catalogue series, C-04); the bar of 4 makes 47 items eligible. One is printed by every paper in print and admitted (General Moreau's report, 5 of 5); 27 others are chosen (28 stories, 28 groups, 115 printings); 18 are listed as not chosen and 1 for the owner.
for_user_decision.Choosing among the eligible items (X-179: As built: the eligible items are taken in order of their papers and first printing, and each is chosen unless an item of the same affair, as the reading names it, is already chosen within a month of it (X-1800-01). So the year keeps one story of the war in Europe every second or third month (the Rhine in February, Pichegru in May, Italy in July, General Moreau's report in October), one of the Algiers affair (the Sophia, 5 papers), and one of the Royalists in France (the Cher, 5 papers). No item is eligible in March, November or December.
for_user_decision.Items printed in their own words (X-1796: As built (C-02): seven printings, one in each of seven stories, print the item in the paper's own words or without its lead (the elephant, Captain Atkinson, Captain Seward, the Baron de Carondelet, the ratifications, the papers on a general peace, General Moreau's letter); each is counted with the item and its excerpt starts where that paper's item starts. Without them, six of these stories would have 3 papers.
for_user_decision.Private persons (X-1796-03): As built (R-04): one eligible item turns on a private person (a carter's cruelty to his horse, New York, May, 4 of 6) and is listed for the owner without names; five more items that turn on private persons are below the bar and listed without names.
for_user_decision.Data issues (X-1796-04): As built: the New Hampshire Gazette of 16 April (No. 2055) is filed twice, under 9 and 16 April, so its issue of 9 April does not survive; the ledger uses the 16 April keys, and the in-print counts treat the 9 April filing as a second copy. RevX reads the Patowmac Guardian of 14 April as 'TUESDAY' (a Thursday). The Gazette of the United States stands under two catalogue numbers (C-04). The Patowmac Guardian of 12 May has its RevX transcriptions shifted by one page (the text filed as page 2 is page 3's), which the release's map does not list; the Spain and England printing is on page 3 and its excerpt is cut from the CA text there. A filing correction can re-file that issue's RevX pages.
